classification: one-shot construction boundary probe; not upstream transport test, #3489, or #3311 integrated allocation
hypothesis: A Linux container writing a root-owned mode-0600 IPC-style file onto a Windows-backed Docker Desktop bind mount will leave it readable by the WSL host user, avoiding the specific cross-boundary permission failure seen on WSL ext4.
test: One container invocation creates a unique request fixture at /ipc/request.json with mode 0600 and reports in-container UID/GID/mode/hash. After exit, the WSL host verifies the exact bytes/hash, observed DrvFS mode/owner, and whether the non-root host process can open it.

decision.pass: The WSL non-root process reads the exact 0600-created bytes and hash matches; record DrvFS metadata as observed, without inferring POSIX ACL equivalence.
decision.stop: Any mount, container, metadata, read, hash, or cleanup discrepancy; retain first outcome and do not retry this allocation.

limits: Does not execute repository broker/runner or prove full IPC round trip
Uses a different cached image because upstream test image tag is absent
Does not establish OrbStack behavior or solve #3311's six-task matched efficiency comparison
A host read PASS would support only this Windows-backed mount permission boundary
